brief.scope: Work order: the uncited-correction gate. The requirements are the ten numbered Contract items of .dev/ladder-inputs/scope-gate-20260910.md, tracked in this snapshot at the ref; read it and .dev/ladder-inputs/scope-discipline.md WHOLE from the snapshot tree. Nothing else is a requirement. Refuse at mint any write job that answers reviewer findings unless every finding it answers is named by key, disposed in the findings ledger, and the disposition cites the numbered contract item it violates; the ladder stops before its fix stages instead of correcting. No override. Boundaries as listed there; do not widen them.

findings.claim: Contract items 2, 3, and 8: the sole multi-answer case puts the open key first. An implementation validating and recording only answers[0] passes while admitting an undisposed later answer.
Contract item 1: correction classification covers only adversarial-review and check-tests. An allowlist omitting security-audit, adjudicate, and sweep passes while those corrections bypass the gate.

Contract items 3 and 6: existing planted-store rows are never snapshotted around a gate check. A gate that rewrites or auto-disposes a row after producing the asserted refusal passes, allowing a later attempt through without the commanded disposition.
Contract item 7: the shared non-correction assertion accepts an arguments refusal at exit 2. An implementation refusing every non-correction therefore passes.
findings.reproduce: python3 -B -c 'import importlib.util,types,pathlib; p=pathlib.Path("ops/conductor/tests/test_correction.py"); s=importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("tc",p); m=importlib.util.module_from_spec(s); s.loader.exec_module(m); t=m.NonCorrections("test_write_following_nothing_is_not_a_correction"); t._assert_not_a_correction(types.SimpleNamespace(returncode=2,stdout="",stderr="arguments: expected x; found y; needed z")); print("SURVIVED")'

findings.claim: Contract items 4 and 9: cited is never exercised with parseable evidence naming a missing item or the wrong scope. A cited implementation accepting any parseable contract-item evidence passes while incorrectly releasing the ladder.
Contract item 4: item 3 is the only satisfying citation tested against the named scope. A parser/holder hard-coded for item 3 passes while rejecting valid items 1, 2, and 4-10.
Contract item 4: no correction-gate test proves that correction.py reads CITATION, parse_citation, or citation_holds from findings.py. A private duplicated regex passes, leaving two definitions.
findings.reproduce: python3 -B -c 'from pathlib import Path; s=Path("ops/conductor/tests/test_correction.py").read_text(); print({x:s.count(x) for x in ("citation_holds","parse_citation","CITATION")})'

findings.claim: Contract item 3: needed clauses are checked only by fragments and never compared or executed. A command missing its disposition, evidence, or scope path passes.
Contract item 4: no rejection case places comma or semicolon at the citation-path boundary. The broken pattern `[^\s:]+` survives in place of `[^\s:;,]+`.
findings.reproduce: python3 -B -c 'import ast; from pathlib import Path; t=ast.parse(Path("ops/conductor/tests/test_findings_citation.py").read_text()); v=[n.value for n in ast.walk(t) if isinstance(n,ast.Constant) and isinstance(n.value,str) and "contract item " in n.value]; b=[x for x in v if " of " in x and any(c in x.split(" of ",1)[1].split(":",1)[0] for c in ",;")]; print(b); raise SystemExit(bool(b))'

envelope.note: Both suites failed red on their intended assertions: 29/29 and 18/18 failures, with no errors. The plant guard passed. Report sha256: ab64244ecb57e4eec5b650c4f4a42871710fb67c59098ac222b7dc2e685ca0b6.
